newsitem.title: USA: House passes $12 billion transport bill.
newsitem.headline: House passes $12 billion transport bill.

text.p: The U.S. House of Representatives on Wednesday passed by a 424-5 vote a $12.48 billion transportation spending bill for fiscal 1998, including a nearly 20 percent increase in highway spending and new air safety initiatives.
The bill was very close to President Bill Clinton's $12.47 billion budget request, and was $400 million above the spending in the current fiscal year.
The bill includes funding for the Federal Aviation Administration to, among other things, install new airport security devices and improve storm and weather detection systems.
It also adds 500 air traffic controllers, and 326 FAA staff for safety certification and regulation.
The bill also would add money for the Coast Guard's efforts to combat drug trafficking, and targets Amtrak funding to improve the Northeast corridor.
